figures.alt: Four small icons in a row with sound waves: snoring (tongue against the pharynx), gurgling (fluid in the throat), stridor (a narrowed upper airway), wheeze (narrowed small bronchi).
An adult giving the universal choking sign, both hands clutching the throat.
An oropharyngeal airway (OPA) and a nasopharyngeal airway (NPA) side by side, with their parts labeled (flange, bevel, curve).
Four close-ups: raccoon eyes, Battle's sign behind the ear, seat-belt bruise across the abdomen, flail segment moving inward on inspiration.
An oxygen cylinder strapped upright in an ambulance, with a no-smoking / no-flame symbol nearby.
Over-ventilation shown as cause and effect: a forceful squeeze leads to air in the stomach, a swollen abdomen, then regurgitation.
An unresponsive patient who is vomiting, rolled onto the side so the fluid drains.

figures.section: Which artery, which wall, what to expect
figures.alt: The heart's surface with the LAD, circumflex and right coronary arteries drawn in three colors, each shading the wall it feeds.
Three people side by side (an older woman, an older man, a person checking their blood glucose), each with a speech bubble: "just tired", "indigestion", "short of breath".

figures.section: Treat the organ, not the number
figures.alt: A body outline with five highlighted target organs (brain, eyes, heart, aorta, kidneys) and a pregnant abdomen as a sixth, each with a warning icon.
A rescuer kneeling beside the patient, shoulders over the hands, arms straight, heel of the hand on the lower half of the sternum, with a depth gauge showing 5–6 cm and a metronome at 100–120/min.
figures.caption: Depth 5–6 cm, rate 100–120/min.

figures.alt: Four small panels: shaving a hairy chest, drying a wet chest, peeling off a medication patch, and a pad placed beside (not over) an implanted device bulge.
A windlass tourniquet on the thigh 5–7 cm above a wound, not over the knee, with the time written on the tag.
figures.caption: Tourniquet 5–7 cm above the wound, not over a joint. Write the time on the tag.

figures.alt: Wound packing in the groin: gauze pushed deep with two fingers, then both hands pressing with straight arms.
Four icons: a bleeding drop (hypovolemic), a failing heart (cardiogenic), a dilated vessel (distributive), a blocked vessel / collapsed lung (obstructive).
An EMS provider sitting at eye level with a family member in a quiet room, hand open, calm posture.

Six small patient vignettes in a grid: wheezing asthmatic with inhaler, COPD patient with pursed lips and barrel chest, feverish patient coughing, patient clutching the side of the chest after a flight (PE), tall thin young man with one-sided pain (pneumothorax), patient sitting upright with frothy
A small-volume nebulizer with mouthpiece, showing the reservoir, mist and oxygen or air tubing.

Six icons for Balance, Eyes, Face, Arm, Speech, Time: a person swaying, an eye with half the visual field greyed out, a face drooping on one side, one arm drifting down, a speech bubble with jumbled letters, a clock.
A rescuer kneeling beside a seizing person, cushioning the head with a folded jacket, furniture moved away, a watch visible, nothing in the mouth.
The recovery position after a seizure, with airway open.
Three treatments side by side: oral glucose gel, a glucagon kit (vial and syringe) with an IM thigh site, and a nasal glucagon device.
A body outline with the systems affected: swollen lips and tongue, hives on the skin, wheeze from the lungs, a falling BP gauge, a cramping stomach.
An auto-injector pressed into the outer middle thigh through clothing, with the target area shaded on the anterolateral thigh.
Two positions: lying flat with legs raised (low BP) and sitting up (breathing difficulty), with a crossed-out standing figure.
Two-rescuer BVM ventilation of an unresponsive patient, with a naloxone nasal spray and syringe ready on the floor.
A house with a furnace and a car in the garage, several family members and a pet feeling unwell, a CO alarm.
A forearm with an arteriovenous fistula (raised vein), a crossed-out BP cuff on that arm and the cuff on the other arm instead.
Normal round red cells flowing through a vessel next to sickled cells blocking it, with a pain icon downstream.
A selection of anticoagulant tablet boxes (generic, unbranded) beside a head-injury icon with a CT scanner.
A patient with infection sources highlighted (lungs, urine, abdomen, skin wound) and warning signs around them: confusion, fast breathing, low BP, mottled skin.
The glass test: a clear glass pressed on a non-blanching purple rash that stays visible.
An EMS provider at a safe distance with open hands and calm posture, standing between the patient and the door, a partner nearby.
Correct position: a restrained patient on their side on a stretcher with monitoring; a crossed-out prone figure with weight on the back.
The abdomen divided into four quadrants with the main organs drawn underneath (liver, gallbladder, stomach, spleen, appendix, sigmoid colon), and kidneys and aorta shown behind.
An EMS crew stopping short of a scene and scanning: traffic, a downed power line, a person with a weapon, a leaking fuel puddle, each circled as a hazard.
A patient in a cervical collar on a scoop stretcher and vacuum mattress, beside a long backboard labelled "extrication only".
An EMS provider at eye level with a seated patient, a family member holding a medication bag, and a notepad with SAMPLE written down the side.
Four close-ups: raccoon eyes, Battle's sign behind the ear, seat-belt bruise across the abdomen, flail segment moving inward on inspiration.
A cartoon EMS provider with a ship's anchor chained to a thought bubble saying "just a UTI", while a stroke sign (droopy face) is ignored behind them.
An overhead view of a mass-casualty scene with colour-coded treatment areas (red, yellow, green), a command post, a staging area and an ambulance loading point.
The three collisions of a frontal crash in three panels: the car hitting a wall, the driver hitting the steering wheel, the brain and aorta moving inside the body.
Wound packing in the groin: gauze pushed deep with two fingers, then both hands pressing with straight arms.
A body outline highlighting the five bleeding sites: the floor (external), chest, abdomen, pelvis/retroperitoneum and thighs.
An amputated finger wrapped in moist gauze, sealed in a bag, resting in a container of ice water; a crossed-out finger directly on ice.
A knife stabilised in the thigh with rolled bulky dressings on both sides, taped in place.
A skin cross-section with superficial, partial-thickness and full-thickness burn depths marked.
A face with one fixed, dilated pupil and a monitor showing rising BP and falling heart rate.
A scoop stretcher being closed around a supine patient wearing a collar, one rescuer holding in-line stabilisation at the head.
A splinted forearm with fingers exposed and a rescuer checking capillary refill and finger movement.
A team of three working in parallel on one patient: one at the airway with a BVM, one tightening a tourniquet, one applying a pelvic binder, an ambulance waiting with doors open.
McRoberts manoeuvre: two helpers pulling the mother's knees towards her chest while a third presses just above the pubic bone with the heel of the hand.
One hand cupping the fundus above the umbilicus and massaging in circles, the other hand just above the pubic bone supporting the lower uterus.
Clothing items each placed in a separate brown paper bag, labelled and sealed, next to a patient wrapped in a blanket.
A newborn bag-mask with the mask covering mouth and nose but not the eyes, held with a C-grip, and a pulse oximeter probe on the right wrist.
Side by side: a toddler with croup coughing on a parent's lap, and a child with epiglottitis sitting forward in tripod position, drooling, mouth open.
An older woman on a living-room floor beside a rug, a clock on the wall, with callouts for pressure areas on the hip and heel.
A table covered in pill boxes and a weekly organiser, with a rescuer bagging all the medicines to bring to hospital.
A rescuer facing a deaf patient in good light while a sign language interpreter appears on a tablet video call.
A forearm with an arteriovenous fistula (raised vein), a crossed-out BP cuff on that arm and the cuff on the other arm instead.
Two-person bag-mask: one rescuer with both hands sealing the mask (thumbs on the mask, fingers lifting the jaw), the other squeezing the bag.
A team of six using an air-assisted transfer mat to move a patient from a bed to a bariatric cot, patient covered with a sheet.

A horizontal chain of six linked icons: a bystander with a phone, a dispatcher with a headset, an ambulance, a clipboard of protocols with a doctor, a hospital, and a looping arrow for quality review.
Overhead view of a highway: a fire engine angled upstream as a block, cones tapering traffic, the ambulance beyond it, crew in high-visibility vests working on the protected side.
A tanker with a placard, with a wind arrow and an ambulance parked upwind, uphill and at a distance; hot, warm and cold zones shaded.
Three simple figures: one with a racing heart after a call (acute), one waking from a nightmare weeks later (delayed), one slumped and drained over a calendar of shifts (burnout).
A hand being washed under running water with soap after a needlestick, with crossed-out icons for squeezing and bleach.
Trauma shears cutting around a bullet hole in a shirt, and the shirt going into a brown paper evidence bag.
A paramedic kneeling at eye level with a seated patient, explaining with an open hand, a refusal form and pen on a clipboard between them.
A "hands-off" handover in an emergency bay: the paramedic speaking while the hospital team stands around the stretcher listening, hands at their sides.
Side view of a power lift: squatting provider with feet shoulder-width apart, straight back, load close; a second figure bending at the waist crossed out.
A clothes drag: a rescuer pulling a patient by the shirt at the shoulders along the long axis, the patient's head supported between the forearms, smoke in the background.
An athlete immersed to the neck in a tub of ice water at a sports field, one rescuer supporting the head and stirring the water, another holding a rectal thermometer readout.
An older patient on a stretcher stripped to underwear, being misted with a spray bottle while a fan blows across, ice packs at the neck, armpits and groin.
Reach, throw, row, go: four small panels – a pole, a throw bag, a boat, and a trained swimmer with a flotation device.
A rescuer on a pool deck giving bag-mask breaths to a child, foam at the mouth, suction ready beside them.
Overhead view of a spill with red hot zone, yellow warm zone containing a decontamination corridor, and green cold zone with the ambulance and command post upwind.
Two body outlines comparing rashes: smallpox densest on face and limbs with all lesions alike, chickenpox mainly on the trunk with lesions at different stages.
An overhead view of a mass-casualty scene with colour-coded treatment areas (red, yellow, green), a command post, a staging area and an ambulance loading point.
A receptor drawn as a lock: an agonist key turning it (light on), an antagonist key sitting in it but not turning (light off), and a partial agonist half-turning it.
A neatly organised drug pouch with labelled slots: aspirin, nitroglycerin spray, oral glucose, epinephrine auto-injector, naloxone nasal spray, albuterol nebules.
Three receptor diagrams: methadone fully activating, buprenorphine partly activating with a "ceiling" line, naltrexone blocking.
Two-person bag-mask: one rescuer with both hands sealing the mask (thumbs on the mask, fingers lifting the jaw), the other squeezing the bag.
Wound packing in the groin: gauze pushed deep with two fingers, then both hands pressing with straight arms.
A sling and swath on a seated patient, padding in the armpit, the swath binding the arm to the chest.
A landing zone with lit corners, wind indicator, a power line marked as a hazard, and the safe approach arc at the front of the helicopter, tail and uphill sides crossed out.
An auto-injector pressed into the outer middle thigh through clothing, with the target area shaded on the anterolateral thigh.
A syringe with an atomiser tip delivering a fine mist into one nostril, labelled "half in each side".
Three treatments side by side: oral glucose gel, a glucagon kit (vial and syringe) with an IM thigh site, and a nasal glucagon device.
A medicine capsule with four icons for the drug groups: heart, lungs, syringe and IV bag.
